subject.statement: Markus Braun, former CEO of Wirecard

summary: Markus Braun, former CEO of Wirecard AG, led the company from January 2002 until his resignation in June 2020, was arrested shortly thereafter, and has remained in pre‑trial detention while awaiting trial on charges of fraud, breach of trust, and accounting manipulation filed in March 2022. He has not been convicted, and a Munich Regional Court has ordered him and other former board members to pay EUR 140 million in damages plus interest. The criminal trial commenced in 2022 and continues, but its expected conclusion, the enforcement status of the civil judgment, and any ongoing regulatory sanctions are not established by the current evidence.

findings.statement: Markus Braun served as CEO of Wirecard AG from January 2002 until his resignation in June 2020.
Markus Braun resigned as CEO on 19 June 2020.
In March 2022, Markus Braun was formally charged with fraud, breach of trust, and accounting manipulation related to Wirecard AG.
Markus Braun has not been convicted of any criminal offense related to Wirecard; he pleads not guilty and awaits trial.
As of December 2022, criminal proceedings against Markus Braun were ongoing and he was in pre‑trial detention.
A Munich Regional Court judgment ordered Markus Braun and other former board members to pay EUR 140 million in damages plus interest (Judgment of September 5, 2024).
The Munich criminal trial for fraud and falsifying accounts against Markus Braun began in 2022 and is ongoing.

gaps: The expected timeline or projected conclusion of Markus Braun's criminal trial is not disclosed in the available sources.
Details on the enforcement or collection status of the EUR 140 million civil judgment against Markus Braun are not provided in the evidence.
No information concerning ongoing regulatory sanctions or bans imposed on Markus Braun by German financial authorities appears in the reviewed sources.
